input.command: ls; cat CLAUDE.md; cat -n src/routes.ts; ls src
input.description: List repo and read routes file

input.command: cat -n src/worktree.ts src/store.ts src/api.ts src/config.ts; grep -rn "template\|cacheListing\|registerRepo\|validate" src
input.description: Read related files and grep route usage

input.reason: Nothing in the repository checks the repository id. registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18-23) only checks that `id` and `remoteUrl` are non-empty. It saves the id and passes it to cloneRepo. cloneRepo calls cachePath (src/worktree.ts:9-11), which returns `path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, id)`. An id such as `../../../tmp/x` or `/tmp/x` therefore sends the git clone to a directory outside /var/harbor/repos. The template route (src/routes.ts:35-40) builds `base` from the raw `req.params.id`. Its `startsWith(base)` check only compares the file path against that base, which the attacker also controls. If the id resolves to a higher directory, the check still passes and the route reads any file under that directory. cacheListing (line 60) resolves the raw id with the same cachePath helper. Store.insertRepo stores the id as given, and no other file contains validation or router middleware. CLAUDE.md is not in the working tree, so F14's appeal to "invariant 1" has no support. The missing validation it describes is still real.
input.failure_scenario: A user calls the template route with id `../../..` (URL-encoded if the router needs it) and name `../etc/passwd`. `base` becomes `/`, `file` resolves to `/etc/passwd`, `startsWith("/")` passes, and the route returns the file's contents. With id `..` and name `../audit.log`, the same route returns /var/harbor/audit.log, which bypasses the admin IP check in auditLog. Separately, POST registerRepo with body id `/tmp/evil` clones the attacker's repository to /tmp/evil instead of a folder under /var/harbor/repos.
input.severity_reason: This is a security flaw that can be exploited: a caller can read files anywhere on the server and write clones outside /var/harbor/repos. I rated it High rather than Critical because the router and authentication layer are not in the repository. How URL params are decoded and who can reach these routes cannot be confirmed from the code. The registerRepo write outside the repositories directory uses the request body, so it does not depend on the router.
